newsitem.title: UK: UK researchers find biological link to anorexia.
newsitem.headline: UK researchers find biological link to anorexia.

text.p: British researchers say they have found a brain abnormality which may be a cause of anorexia, the eating disorder which has afflicted Princess Diana and causes sufferers to starve themselves, sometimes to death.

A team of researchers at London's Great Ormond Street children's hospital said most anorexia sufferers they studied had reduced blood flow in an area of the brain which governs visual perception and appetite. The researchers were due to present the findings at a London conference on Tuesday.
Bryan Lask, a consultant psychiatrist at the hospital, said the discovery could be a first step in finding a cure for the condition.
"If we can find exactly what this abnormality represents, an abnormality in biochemistry in the brain cells, we may eventually be able to reverse that," he told BBC radio.
Lask said the brain abnormality was probably one of several causes of anorexia, along with psychological and social factors.

"We believe the possibility is it's genetically determined. People are born with this predisposition and then other factors come into play," he said. "They all come into play around the time of puberty, that's when the condition starts."
The brain abnormality affected visual perception and could explain why anorexia sufferers believed themselves to be fat even though many are dangerously thin, Lask said.

"It's in the part of the brain which processes our visual images," he said. "So when we look at ourselves in the mirror normally we'd see what we really look like. But this abnormality distorts what we see."
Lask said the discovery would help sufferers, who would no longer be regarded as "mad or bad".

"We can say to people with anorexia nervosa -- this is not your fault, you're not making it up," Lask said. "Parents can be helped by saying to them that it's not their fault, this is something you're born with."
